title: The 10 Best Rivet Guns
subtitle: Manual pop rivet guns and hand riveters for sheet metal, gutters, trailers and auto work, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A hand rivet gun sets blind (pop) rivets from one side of the work, so it joins sheet metal, gutters, trailer skins and plastic where you can't reach the back. We ranked 10 best-sellers on rating, review volume and features (1/4-inch capacity, rivets and drill bits in the box, a case and a warranty of a year or more). Most one-hand guns top out at 3/16-inch rivets; for 1/4-inch and stainless rivets, buy a long-handle two-hand riveter. They run from about $14 to $73.

avoid.name: Arrow RHT300 One-Handed Swivel Rivet Tool, Manual Riveter
avoid.flag: Listing says all steel; spec table says plastic
avoid.verdict: A swivel-head riveter whose listing can't agree on what it's made of, with the lowest rating of the riveters we looked at. Arrow's own RH200 kit costs about $4 more and includes 120 rivets.
reasons: A bullet promises 'rugged all steel construction', while the spec table lists the material as plastic.
Another bullet describes 'the anti-slip handle on the rivet nut tool', but this is a blind-rivet tool, not a rivet nut tool, so the copy looks pasted from another product.
It's rated 3.9 stars, the lowest of the riveters we compared, and no rivets come in the box.

buyers_guide.q: What size rivet gun do I need?
buyers_guide.a: Match the gun to the rivet diameter. Most one-hand guns take 3/32, 1/8, 5/32 and 3/16-inch rivets, which covers gutters, flashing and light auto work. For 1/4-inch rivets on trailers and truck bodies, get a long-handle two-hand riveter like the Astro 1423 or NEXTACK NT300.

buyers_guide.q: Can a hand riveter set steel or stainless rivets?
buyers_guide.a: Aluminum rivets are easy. Steel and stainless take much more force: Arrow says not to use 3/16-inch steel or any stainless rivets in its manual tools, while the long-handle Astro and NEXTACK are rated for 1/4-inch stainless. Check the listing before you buy rivets.

buyers_guide.q: How long should the rivet be?
buyers_guide.a: The rivet's grip range has to cover the total thickness of the parts you're joining. Too short and it won't set; too long and it sets loose. Kits with several lengths, like the NEXTACK's eight sizes, make it easier to match thick stacks.

buyers_guide.q: What drill bit do I use?
buyers_guide.a: Drill a hole just over the rivet diameter, usually the bit listed for that rivet size. Kits from WETOLS, LIBRATON, GIANTISAN and KLRStec include a bit for each rivet size.

buyers_guide.q: Is a rivet gun the same as a rivet nut tool?
buyers_guide.a: No. A rivet gun sets blind rivets, which are permanent. A rivet nut tool sets threaded inserts you can bolt into. The Astro and NEXTACK listings both note they're not for rivet nuts.
